# The ORC — Plan (2026-11-18)

> Copied from the Obsidian vault note `7 - Dev Folder/1. Projects/Orca/2026-11-18 - Plan v2 - Spaces and Missions.md` before any build work started. `[[…]]` links point to notes in that vault.

**What this is.** A desktop app where you **talk to a real Claude Code session**, exactly like a normal terminal session. That session is a mission's **coordinator**: it spawns worker agents, each one a real Claude Code session in its own git worktree.
- A tree on the right branches every time an agent is spawned. Clicking a branch shows that agent's terminal, and you can type into it.
- Status cards on the left show what every agent is doing.
- Work is organised into **Spaces** (one per repository) and **Missions** (one coordinator each). There can be several missions in the same repo, for example "UI revamp" next to "Social feed", and several spaces open at once.

This replaces [[2026-11-18 - Plan - Orca Mission Control]] (v1). v1 used one-shot `claude -p` workers and buttons in place of conversation. The owner rejected that model on 2026-11-18: they want to talk to the sessions and type into them.

Draft for review. No tickets and no ADR exist yet.

Each item is tagged with where it comes from:
- **[Orca]**: the existing Orca.
- **[stably]**: stablyai/orca.
- **[CC]**: built into Claude Code.
- **[Aug]**: [[2026-08-11 - Grilling - Autonomous Orca]].
- **[new]**: new in this plan.

## The layout

```
┌─ Spaces ─────────┬──────────── Terminal ─────────────┬─ Mission tree ───┐
│ ▾ RecipeApp      │                                   │  ● Coordinator   │
│   ▸ UI revamp    │  > build the social feed: posts,  │  ├─● navbar      │
│   ▾ Social feed  │    likes, follows                 │  ├─● post-api    │
│     ┌──────────┐ │  ● Splitting into 3 workers…      │  │ └─○ tests     │
│     │post-api  │ │                                   │  └─◐ follows     │
│     │editing   │ │  (click a tree node → this pane   │                  │
│     │routes.cs │ │   shows that agent's terminal,    │  ● working       │
│     │42k tok   │ │   and you can type into it)       │  ◐ needs you     │
│     └──────────┘ │                                   │  ○ queued/idle   │
│ ▸ Orca           │                                   │                  │
└──────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────┘
```

- **Left: Spaces → Missions → status cards** [stably].
  - Each card shows the agent's name, its state, its current activity (taken from its last tool call), its token use, its branch and the instruction it was given most recently.
- **Middle: the terminal** of whichever agent is selected. By default that's the mission's coordinator.
- **Right: the mission tree** [new].
  - A node appears whenever any agent spawns a worker, so workers can have sub-workers.
  - Node colour shows state. Message lines between nodes can be switched on.
- **Header:** the Space and Mission names, plus **Pause mission**, **Stop mission**, **Merge to main** and the gating mode.

## How each piece works

### 1. Real terminals [stably]
- The app starts each agent with `claude` inside a pseudo-terminal (`node-pty`) and draws it with **xterm.js**.
- Every agent's terminal stays alive in the background. Selecting a tree node only changes which one is shown.
- You type into any of them normally. **Permission prompts work as usual**: a worker waiting on one turns its node ◐ "needs you", and you click in to answer.

### 2. Spawning: the app's `spawn_agent` tool [new]
The app's main process hosts an **HTTP MCP endpoint on `127.0.0.1`** and gives every session its tools: `spawn_agent(name, task)`, `report_done(summary)` and `ask_human(question)`. Each session is started with its own `--mcp-config` carrying a **per-agent bearer token** (`claude mcp` supports HTTP transport with headers, checked on 2.1.327). The token tells the app *which agent* is calling, and that is how the tree knows a new node's parent. *(Corrected 2026-11-18: an earlier draft said stdio. A stdio server is started by `claude`, not by the app, so it has no route back to the app.)*

`spawn_agent` does four things:
1. creates a worktree on `mission/<mission>/<name>`;
2. starts `claude -n <mission>/<name>` in an app-owned terminal, with the task as its first prompt;
3. adds a node to the tree under the agent that called it;
4. returns the new agent's session name.

**Why the app has to do the spawning:** if an agent started workers itself with `claude --bg`, the app would not own those terminals and could not show them to you. The coordinator learns to use `spawn_agent` from a mission prompt added with `--append-system-prompt`.

### 3. Messaging: built into Claude Code [CC], verified 2026-11-18
Agents talk with Claude Code's own `SendMessage` / `ListAgents`, addressing each other by session name. The app does not carry messages; it only **watches** them (see 4) for the feed. Results of a live probe on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.326–2.1.327):
- ✅ **An idle session is woken by a message.** A background session sitting idle received a message and acted on it with no one typing.
- ✅ **`notify_when_idle`** lets the coordinator wait for a worker to finish its turn without polling.
- ✅ **`claude agents --json`** lists every session (name, cwd, session id, busy/idle state), which gives the app a ready-made status source.
- ⚠️ **Permission modes must match.** A session in a different permission mode **held** the message for a human to approve (*"The sending session's permission mode class doesn't match … set `crossSessionInbound` to `accept`"*). So every session in a mission starts in the same mode, or the app sets `crossSessionInbound: "accept"` in each session's settings. The **sender** is told in each case: a "held" notice, then an "expired" notice once nobody approved it. A held message to a background session **expires undelivered**, because nobody is there to approve it. The feed should show these states (held / expired) and not just "sent".
- ⚠️ **A new folder must be trusted** before a session can start there (*"Workspace not trusted. Run `claude` … once and accept the trust prompt"*). Every new worktree is a new folder, so check in M1 whether worktrees placed inside the already-trusted repo (e.g. `<repo>/.missions/…`) inherit its trust. If they don't, the app needs a way to pre-trust them.
- A sent message isn't guaranteed to be read. It arrives at the receiver's next tool call. The feed shows "delivered", not "done".
- One thing to look into in M1: Claude Code's own *teams* (`ListAgents` mentions "teammates on your team"). If teams can run in terminals the app hosts, they could replace `spawn_agent`.

### 4. Status: hooks [stably + CC]
- Each session gets hook settings through `--settings` that send events to the app: tool use, turn finished, waiting for permission, `SendMessage` calls. stablyai uses the same approach (`src/main/agent-hooks/`).
- **`claude agents --json`** is the backup when hooks are silent.
- To check in M1: do hooks passed with `--settings` fire **alongside** your own hooks, or replace them?

### 5. Token use on the cards
- Interactive sessions don't print a cost summary. But each session's transcript JSONL (`~/.claude/projects/<dir>/<session-id>.jsonl`) carries `usage` on every message. **Verified.**
- The cards show tokens, and the mission header sums them.
- Every session in every mission shares **one subscription window**, which is the main practical limit. The app needs a **per-space cap on live agents** and **Pause mission**.

### 6. When you type into a worker [new]
- Your typing and the coordinator's messages land in the same session, so the card shows **who gave the last instruction** ("you, 2 min ago" or "coordinator, 30 s ago").
- Typing into a worker also tells the coordinator, through the app (*"the human is steering post-api directly"*), so it doesn't overwrite you.

### 7. Git: agents never commit [Orca]
- Each session's `--settings` carries `permissions.deny` for git write commands (deny rules work without `--safe-mode`), plus your global `deniedTools`.
- When a worker calls `report_done`, **the app commits** its worktree with a structured message.
- The app merges into **`integration/<mission>`** in dependency order, then runs the repo's build/test gate on the merged result.
- A conflict sends a ◐ question to the coordinator, or to you.
- **`main` changes only when you press Merge to main.** That screen shows the **combined diff** of the mission, the gate results and the Verifier report.

### 8. A Verifier before merge [Orca, the idea that survives]
- Before a mission's Merge to main is offered, the app runs **one one-shot Verifier**. It's a scoped `claude -p` run (Orca's role and prompt idea) that checks the combined diff against the coordinator's split and the original brief.
- This is the one place Orca's reproducibility discipline still applies: a pinned prompt, a recorded hash, a written report.

### The vault (D4 suggestion)
The vault is **optional per Space**, and it holds **records, never state**. The app's own state (sessions, tree, worktrees) stays in the app.

- **Writing (the app, at milestones, append-only):** one note per mission at `<vault>/7 - Dev Folder/1. Projects/<Space>/Missions/<date> - <mission>.md`. It records:
  - the brief;
  - the approved split;
  - each worker's `report_done` summary;
  - decisions taken in `ask_human` answers;
  - the Verifier report;
  - the final merge (commit SHA);
  - every session id, so a mission can be reopened with `--resume`.
- **Reading (optional):**
  - a mission can start **from a vault note** (a spec or roadmap written while grilling);
  - a new coordinator is given **links to that Space's past mission notes**, so it knows what was built before and why.
- **Why:**
  - transcripts aren't readable;
  - worktrees are deleted after merge;
  - the mission note is the only lasting "what was done and why";
  - it is August requirement #6.
- **Rules:**
  - only the app writes, which avoids Obsidian Sync conflicts;
  - append only (the vault has no history);
  - keep to the Dev Folder conventions (date header, marked AI-generated).

### Gating (D3, confirmed 2026-11-18)
| Mode | What it means with live sessions |
|---|---|
| **Checkpointed** | Every worker's `report_done` stops for **your review of that worker's diff** before it merges into the integration branch |
| **Plan check** (default) | The coordinator presents its split by calling `propose_split`, and you approve it in the UI. After that, finished workers merge into the integration branch on their own |
| **No check** | Workers merge into the integration branch on their own, with no split approval |

In every mode, **Merge to main is your click**.

**`propose_split` must not hold the coordinator until you click.** MCP calls can time out; check Claude Code's limit rather than assuming one. The tool returns "pending" straight away, and your approval reaches the coordinator later as a message.

**This still needs an ADR.** Even plan check (the default) lets work merge into the integration branch without a human, which overturns kickoff §10 ("no cross-checkpoint autonomy"). Approving this plan triggers that ADR, as in v1. [[BF-10 - Prompt injection paths into the judges]] matters for the Verifier in §8.

## The stack (be honest about it)

- **A new repo.** TypeScript throughout: **Electron + React + Vite**, with **node-pty + xterm.js** for the terminals, **shadcn/ui + Tailwind** for the look, **React Flow** for the tree, and **Motion** for animation. Electron is the safe choice on Linux/Wayland; stablyai proves it works there.
- **What survives from Orca's .NET code:** very little *code*. The **ideas** survive: agents never commit, integration branches, the gating modes, the Verifier role and its prompt, vault records, and the denied-tools list.
- **The pinned-contract and `--safe-mode` guarantees no longer cover the sessions.** Workers are normal Claude Code: your CLAUDE.md, plugins and MCP servers load into every worker. That's the point (it's "the Claude Code I use"), but it does change what's guaranteed.
- If D1 ends up as "fork stablyai", most of this stack comes ready-made, and the work becomes adding spaces/missions, the tree, gating and the Verifier.

---

## Safety

- **The local endpoints are a control surface.**
  - The MCP endpoint and the hook receiver listen on `127.0.0.1` only, and each agent has **its own token**: a request without a valid token is rejected, and a token only acts as its own agent.
  - The hook receiver listens on `127.0.0.1` only and requires a **token generated at each launch**, because a forged hook event could fake a status or an approval.
- **Recovery after a crash.** On restart the app reconciles before it does anything else:
  - it finds orphaned `claude` processes and terminals;
  - it reattaches each tree node to its session with `claude --resume <session-id>`, since every node stores its session id;
  - it keeps dirty worktrees and lists them.
- **Permissions aren't passed between sessions** [CC]. A worker can't get around a denied command by asking another session to run it. Keep it that way.

## Milestones

**M0: decide D1–D4.** Including a day of using stablyai's app on a real task.

**M1: the core, with no polish.**
- An Electron window: one Space, one Mission.
- A real coordinator terminal.
- `spawn_agent` creating worktrees and terminals.
- A plain list in place of the tree, where clicking switches terminals.
- Status from hooks and `claude agents --json`.
- Answer the M1 checks: worktree trust, hook layering, Claude Code teams, and the MCP timeout.
- *Progress 2026-11-18:* the launch flags, the HTTP MCP endpoint with per-agent tokens, and hook delivery are verified with a real session (see `docs/HANDOFF.md`). 
- *Done 2026-11-19 (overnight):* verified end to end by `tests/e2e.sh` (hidden window, Haiku). Worktrees inherit trust, `--settings` hooks layer on top of the user's, and status also polls `claude agents --json`. Teams are deferred (experimental, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`). The MCP tool timeout is a hard wall-clock limit, set by `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` or per server. See `docs/HANDOFF.md`.
- *Done when:* you ask the coordinator for a two-part task, two workers appear, you click into one and type to it, and both report done.

**M2: the real UI.**
- Spaces → Missions → status cards on the left.
- The React Flow tree on the right, with live state.
- The message feed and token counts.
- Several missions per space, and several spaces.

**M3: git and gates.**
- Agents can't commit; the app commits on `report_done`.
- Integration branch per mission, merge-result gate, conflicts as questions.
- Gating modes and `propose_split`.
- The Merge to main screen with the combined diff.
- The Verifier.

**M4: robustness.**
- Recovery after a crash, the live-agent cap, Pause mission.
- The localhost token, and writing mission records to the vault.

**Later:** an integration agent that resolves conflicts, GitHub/Linear as sources for missions, agents other than Claude.
